source.title: Strategy Coopetition Explains the Emergence and Transience of In-Context Learning
source.authors: Aaditya K. Singh; Ted Moskovitz; Sara Dragutinovic; Felix Hill; Stephanie C. Y. Chan; Andrew M. Saxe

page_placements.theme: ICL transience and competition with in-weights learning

record.tranche_reason: The study investigates induction circuits and in-context learning dynamics, and refines the account: the Layer 2 induction circuit is reused in a different strategy while Layer 1 changes, and ICL can be transient or persistent depending on setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports relevant behavioral evaluations, attention-pattern measurements, causal ablations and training interventions. Figure-only timecourses are included where their outcomes are described in the text. Results cited from other studies are not rows.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (2-layer attention-only transformers on bursty Omniglot few-shot data), the study shows ICL running through a Layer 1 previous-token plus Layer 2 induction-head circuit. Blocking previous-token attention or using one layer prevents ICL (V1). Emergence and persistence depend on data, positional embeddings and training history (V5), and timing is stable across seeds (V4). Its central novelty is that induction heads persist but get reused by a non-ICL strategy (CIWL), which fits no version directly.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that ICL is transient because it is replaced by context-constrained in-weights learning (CIWL). ICL and CIWL share the Layer 2 induction heads, which cooperatively enable ICL's emergence, and compete in Layer 1, which switches from previous-token to self-attention. ICL emerges only if CIWL is not yet formed. Matching context and query exemplars makes ICL persistent, also in a 12-layer model.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a synthetic Omniglot few-shot task and behavioral evaluators, attention-pattern measurements and causal interventions in small transformers; it does not reproduce the original broad language-model loss-by-token analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: ICL behavior varies with positional-embedding type, class and exemplar counts, initialization seed, context/query exemplar matching, MLP use and training checkpoint/history.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer 2 induction heads persist largely unchanged after formation but are reused by a non-ICL strategy (CIWL) once Layer 1 switches from previous-token to self-attention. Induction-head attention thus outlives ICL, and ICL is transient.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction heads can remain while in-context learning disappears, because their role depends on upstream Layer 1 heads; induction-head presence is not equivalent to ICL.

fits_no_version.finding: The end-of-training CIWL strategy uses skip-trigram copying in Layer 2 heads, with K- and V-composition to Layer 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The asymptotic strategy reuses induction-head composition for context-constrained in-weights learning.

record.problems: The main mechanistic and behavioral evidence comes from a minimal synthetic task and small models. Several outcomes are presented as plots without numeric values or uncertainty estimates. The authors describe their superposition explanation as speculative and preliminary. The claimed later-token loss signature is not measured.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results within the 60-row limit were left out.

untested.parts: Abruptness and narrow-window timing are not quantified; no training-loss bump or loss-versus-token-index measure; induction-head formation is not timed against ICL onset numerically.
Entirely untested: no large models and no token-index loss.
Other model families, sizes, modalities and architectures with induction-head inspection; only seeds are varied with an ICL-behaviour proxy.
Large pretrained language models; natural-language few-shot tasks.
Not tested: sub-steps of induction-head formation itself are not resolved. The ICL-to-CIWL switch happens after formation.

missing.what: At ICL-peak checkpoints, ablating Layer 1 heads 1, 4 and 7 drops the ICL evaluator to chance.
Clamping Layer 2 to end-of-training weights reproduces behaviour after the initial phase change (Layer 2 stable); fixing Layer 1 freezes behaviour.
On ICL-only data from scratch, the network sits on a long loss plateau before learning ICL.
Layer 1 head 1 shows transient previous-token attention over training.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V7 support label is dropped: the ICL-to-CIWL switch is post-formation, not sub-steps of induction-head formation. Positional-embedding and class-count rows bear on V5, not V4. CIWL-mechanism rows (r3-r8, r27, r28) measure a skip-trigram strategy, not induction. Several results are figure-only and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish the mechanism across model families or beyond the studied synthetic task.
Does not measure later-token loss relative to earlier tokens, or establish that a sharp training-loss bump coincides with ICL gain.
The study does not measure whether induction heads carry most ICL in large transformers, or measure ICL as loss falling with token index.
Does not establish universality across model families, modalities or a broad range of training runs.
Tests selected data properties and training interventions, not an exhaustive set of data and training configurations.
Does not test few-shot task learning across large pretrained language models or compare all possible alternative mechanisms.
Does not establish that induction-head formation itself always consists of several distinct transitions across settings.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Tracked Layer 2 induction strength on Flip-evaluator data over training.
rows.measure: Average attention delta to correct versus incorrect ICL token
rows.value: figure only
rows.note: The text describes induction circuits as emerging and then flipping, matching the later CIWL attention patterns. The figure supplies no extracted numeric values.
rows.check: Figure-only. Layer 2 induction strength emerges, then flips sign on Flip data as Layer 2 serves CIWL. The flip is not absence of induction heads. Remove V2 and V7: no abruptness or sub-step measure.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Inspected Layer 1 and Layer 2 attention patterns and their roles during the ICL-to-CIWL transition.
rows.measure: Layer 1 previous-token versus self-attention; Layer 2 induction-circuit behavior
rows.value: Layer 1 switches from previous-token attention to self-attention; Layer 2 induction heads remain largely unchanged and are reused for CIWL.
rows.note: Authors describe Layer 2 induction heads as part of ICL circuits and report that their role changes with Layer 1. This is evidence for a multi-part transition, not a single circuit forming and remaining an ICL mechanism.
rows.check: Layer 1 previous-token heads plus Layer 2 induction heads implement ICL early. The later Layer 1 switch to self-attention is a post-formation strategy change, not sub-steps of induction-head formation, so V2 and V7 are removed.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measured Layer 2 attention from the query to context tokens on CIWL sequences.
rows.measure: Average attention pattern from query token to context
rows.value: Heads attend to the correct in-context label regardless of which exemplar it is paired with.
rows.note: This is a skip-trigram-like label-copying computation used by CIWL, rather than evidence that the late-training behavior is ICL.
rows.check: End-of-training CIWL skip-trigram attention; not the [A][B]…[A]→[B] induction mechanism.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Ablated Layer 1-to-output connections using a pattern-preserving method.
rows.note: The authors call the drop negligible; this indicates Layer 1 does not directly contribute to output on this late-training CIWL evaluation.
rows.check: CIWL-evaluator ablation at end of training; measures the CIWL mechanism, not induction.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Ablated Layer 1 head outputs while preserving Layer 2 patterns, queries, keys and values except for the named component.
rows.note: The text interprets this as substantial V-composition between layers.
rows.check: V-composition measured for the CIWL strategy, not induction-based ICL.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Ablated Layer 1 head outputs while preserving Layer 2 patterns, queries, values and other components except keys.
rows.note: The text interprets this as substantial K-composition between layers.
rows.check: K-composition measured for CIWL, not induction-based ICL.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Ablated Layer 1 head outputs while preserving Layer 2 patterns, keys, values and other components except queries.
rows.note: The authors describe this as a very small amount of Q-composition, if any.
rows.check: Q-composition measured for CIWL, not induction.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Clamped one Layer 2 head's attention allocation between the correct and incorrect label tokens and passed the head output through the rest of the network.

conditions.value: each Layer 2 head considered in isolation

rows.measure: Relationship between attention weight on correct label and output predictions
rows.value: Nearly perfect correlation, as described in the text; individual numeric values are figure only.
rows.note: Supports causal label copying by Layer 2 heads in the CIWL setting.
rows.check: Label-copying in CIWL sequences; bears on the CIWL mechanism only.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Tracked performance on the ICL evaluator through training.
rows.measure: In-context accuracy on the ICL evaluator
rows.baseline: chance level 0.5 for the plotted in-context evaluators
rows.value: Above-chance performance emerges and later disappears; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The paper reports emergence and transience but does not report the claim's later-token loss measure or a coincident sharp training-loss bump.
rows.check: ICL emerges after a flat period (figure only). Abruptness, window width and the coincident loss bump are not quantified.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Tracked the balance between ICL and CIWL through the Flip evaluator.
rows.measure: Flip-evaluator accuracy; 1.0 indicates pure ICL and 0.0 pure CIWL
rows.value: ICL dominates early, the strategies are roughly balanced, and CIWL later dominates; the shift occurs over a coexistence period of approximately 3e6 to 2e7 sequences seen.
rows.note: Reports a changing strategy balance during training, not a single lasting induction-head transition.
rows.check: ICL-to-CIWL strategy balance (transience), not induction-head formation.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Examined CIWL-evaluator loss over training.
rows.value: The text reports a brief divot in the curve; numeric values are figure only.
rows.note: This is a short nonmonotonicity in CIWL-evaluator loss, not a reported training-loss bump coinciding with the claimed ICL gain.
rows.check: Divot in CIWL-evaluator loss, not the V2 training-loss bump at ICL onset.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared learned absolute, sinusoidal absolute and rotary positional embeddings.
rows.value: ICL emergence reproduced with learned absolute embeddings.
rows.note: The authors state learned absolute embeddings were needed for ICL emergence in their 2-layer attention-only setup.
rows.check: Pairs with r13 to show dependence on positional-embedding choice. Not universality (V4).

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared sinusoidal absolute and rotary positional embeddings with learned absolute embeddings.
rows.value: The text says ICL emergence was not reproduced.
rows.note: The paper reports this as a dependence on positional-embedding setup.
rows.check: Absence of ICL under sinusoidal or RoPE embeddings demonstrates the V5 dependence, so state is observed for V5. Role should be main, not comparator.

rows.value: The text reports no ICL emergence.
rows.note: The authors also report some asymptotic strengthening of pure in-weights mechanisms in this setting.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the main setup over different model-initialization and data-generation/order seeds.
rows.measure: Timing and profile of ICL transience
rows.value: Data seed made little-to-no difference; model initialization changed exact timing but general curve profiles remained similar.
rows.note: The text does not give the number of seeds in this section.
rows.check: Initialization seed shifts timing but the curve profile is preserved; data seed makes little difference. ICL behaviour is used as a proxy; induction heads are not inspected per seed.

source_check.correct: V5: observed; initialization changes transience timing while data seeds have little effect. V4: cannot_determine; the seed comparison measures behavioral evaluator curves, without inspecting induction heads across seeds.
source_check.problem: A shared partial state does not distinguish observed timing dependence from unmeasured cross-seed head universality.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on data where the relevant context exemplar exactly matched the query exemplar.
rows.measure: Flip-evaluator accuracy and persistence of ICL
rows.baseline: standard bursty data with varying context/query exemplars
rows.value: The text reports that ICL becomes asymptotic and persists after emergence; the matched-exemplar curve converges to accuracy one on the Flip evaluator.
rows.note: The text says this intervention leaves CIWL unchanged while making ICL more effective.

rows.subject: 12-layer transformer with MLPs
rows.operation_detail: Applied the matched-exemplar data intervention in the larger-scale setup.
rows.measure: Persistence of ICL on the Flip evaluator
rows.value: The text says the intervention extends to this larger setup; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The authors report the larger-model timescale of transience is much longer; the non-matched run does not show full fading in the plotted interval.
rows.check: The matched-exemplar run persists, but the unmatched 12-layer run does not fade within the plotted window, so the contrast is incomplete. Remove V4.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on ICL-only data, with Layer 2 and unembedding weights clamped to the end-of-training weights from the standard bursty run.

conditions.value: Layer 2 plus unembedding, standard-run end weights

rows.value: The text reports that ICL learns quickly with the clamped weights; exact curve values are figure only.
rows.note: The ICL-only data is designed so CIWL cannot solve the task; the authors interpret the result as evidence that Layer 2 weights developed during CIWL training can enable ICL.
rows.check: Clamped Layer 2 weights from the bursty run let ICL learn fast on ICL-only data. Shows dependence on training history and initialization.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on ICL-only data while clamping Layer 2 and unembedding weights from checkpoints of a CIWL-only run.

conditions.value: approximately 10M to 32M sequences seen in CIWL-only run

rows.value: The text reports ICL can emerge with checkpoints from about 10M to 32M sequences seen, but not with early or late checkpoints.
rows.note: The authors identify a limited checkpoint window in which CIWL-only weights enable subsequent ICL learning.
rows.check: Only CIWL-only checkpoints from about 10M to 32M sequences enable ICL. This demonstrates dependence on training history, so state is observed rather than partial.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Continued training from CIWL-only checkpoints after switching to bursty data.
rows.value: The text reports that CIWL persists with no emergence of ICL.
rows.note: Authors conclude ICL did not emerge after CIWL had fully formed in these later-checkpoint conditions.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Blocked Layer 1 heads from attending to the previous token throughout training on bursty data.
rows.measure: ICL and CIWL/Flip-evaluator behavior over training
rows.value: The text says ICL did not emerge, while CIWL dynamics were similar to standard training.
rows.note: This is an intervention on training dynamics; it supports the authors' conclusion that transient ICL is not necessary for CIWL emergence.
rows.check: Blocking Layer 1 previous-token attention prevents ICL, supporting the V1 mechanism. For V6 the state is reversed: here few-shot ICL runs through the induction circuit.

source_check.correct: V1: observed; blocking Layer 1 previous-token attention prevents ICL. V6: reversed; this few-shot task depends on the induction circuit. Appendix E.2 additionally reports that ablating Layer 1 heads 1, 4 and 7 at ICL-peak checkpoints reduces ICL-evaluator performance to chance.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Clamped Layer 1 heads 1, 4 and 7 off throughout training.
rows.baseline: standard training with the same initialization
rows.value: The text reports ICL still emerges, slightly delayed, and transience is somewhat slower.
rows.note: The authors use this result as evidence against ICL being an initialization artifact.
rows.check: Tests an initialization-artifact hypothesis. ICL emerges with the identified heads removed, presumably via other Layer 1 heads, but composition is not examined.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Ablated all attention heads, leaving the embedding-to-unembedding pathway.
rows.measure: In-context accuracy, interpreted by the authors as comparison accuracy without access to context tokens
rows.note: Shows a smaller pure in-weights contribution alongside the dominant context-dependent mechanism.
rows.check: Measures the embedding-to-unembedding in-weights pathway on CIWL, not induction or few-shot ICL.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the embedding-to-unembedding pathway while preserving attention patterns and values using cached activations.
rows.note: A 2% drop indicates this pathway is auxiliary to the skip-trigram copying mechanism in this evaluation.
rows.check: Measures the auxiliary pathway on CIWL; not V1 or V6.

rows.subject: 1-layer transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the same bursty data to evaluate whether a single layer learns skip-trigram copying.
rows.value: The text reports that it learns CIWL through skip-trigram-like circuits, but ICL does not emerge.
rows.note: This provides an architectural comparison and shows that skip-trigram copying does not require two layers.
rows.check: A 1-layer model learns CIWL but no ICL, consistent with induction requiring cross-layer composition. Not V6.

relation.reason: The study measures circuit behavior and causally intervenes on it, and tests how data, architecture and training history affect ICL emergence and persistence.

tranche.reason: The setting is new, but the results also directly contradict V6 in that setting: induction-circuit interventions eliminate few-shot ICL, and the paper argues for shared circuitry between forms of context use. T5 captures this substantive qualification of a claim version.

source_check.notes: Layer 2 induction heads remain largely unchanged when ICL gives way to CIWL; the strategy switch occurs in Layer 1. Appendix E.2's checkpoint ablation is important missing row evidence; its separate training-time head ablation delays but does not prevent ICL.

statements.correction: Section 5.3/Figure 4b: Layer 2 plus unembedding weights from CIWL-only checkpoints at 9.8M–31.5M sequences enable ICL during clamped ICL-only training; earlier and later checkpoints do not. Section 5.4: later CIWL-only checkpoints also prevent ICL emergence after switching to bursty data.
statements.problem: The checkpoint experiment uses CIWL-only training, which the paper explicitly distinguishes from pure in-weights learning.

statements.correction: Section 2.3: the ICL evaluator replaces training labels with 0 and 1, invalidating stored exemplar-label mappings. Figure 1: in-context accuracy restricts outputs to the two context labels. Persistence is also assessed with the Flip evaluator.
statements.problem: The distinction from token-index loss is correct, but this paper does not define its ICL evaluator as accuracy on held-out classes.

statements.correction: V6: challenges for the tested minimal Omniglot few-shot setting. Appendix E.1: blocking previous-token attention prevents ICL. Appendix E.2: ablating Layer 1 heads 1, 4 and 7 at peak checkpoints eliminates ICL behavior. Large pretrained language models remain untested.
statements.problem: The experimental description is correct, but limits_scope understates an explicitly reversed V6 result in the named condition.
